text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Egypt's official commodities buyer said on Saturday he had bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat, 150,000 tonnes of French soft red wheat and 50,000 tonnes of Australian soft white wheat. One lot of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat was bought for $148 per tonne FOB and the other 50,000 tonnes for $149.49 per tonnes FOB. The shipment period for both purchases were November 18-30.
BARLEY SALE - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade (GECPT) has sold Jordan 150,000 tonnes of barley for November delivery, a GECPT official said. Prices were not disclosed.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria on Monday launched a snap tender for a total of 100,000 tonnes of French and/or U.S. and/or Argentine soft wheat for shipment in the second half of December. It invited traders to submit bids on Monday with results expected at the earliest later in the day. Last week Algeria bought at least 75,000 tonnes of wheat, including two cargoes of Argentine wheat and one of French wheat.

WHEAT TENDER - Pakistan is seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. number two or better soft white wheat for November 12-30 delivery, the buyers' U.S. agent said. Bids will be opened on November 3 at 1100 Pakistan Standard Time and must remain valid until 1800 Pakistan Standard Time the following day.
CORN TENDER - The Philippine state National Food Authority (NFA) said on Friday it would tender for 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn No 2 or its equivalent on October 29.
- Taiwan's CK Group of importers will tender on Tuesday for 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn. It would be for Jan 17-31 delivery from the U.S. Gulf or Feb 1-15 from PNW.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said on Wednesday it was extending until noon(1000 GMT) on November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited tenders by October 29 for 25,000 tonnes feed barley, for Nov 20-Dec 5 shipment from Europe or Nov 10-25 from North America.

MARKET TALK - South Korean and Japanese buyers will probably buy U.S. corn after recent price falls in Chicago and ahead of a steady rise in trans-Pacific freight rates to the end of the year, regional traders said on Monday.
... Chinese enquiries for soybeans and soybean meal thinned slightly as CBOT soybean futures bounced higher on Friday, Far Eastern grains and oilseeds traders said.

... U.S. Agriculture Department has stopped issuing export certificates for wheat shipments to Turkey, and is considering halting export licenses for other commodities headed for Turkey, including corn and soybeans, a USDA official said Monday.
The USDA action was taken Oct 18, and was in response to the recent implemenation by Turkey of a zero-tolerance policy on wheat in regards to a large group of diseases.
